messages.subject: How to input the "column" name in ggplot? thanks
parts:
I have three plots:
# Balance limits by gender and education
d1 <- ggplot(ccdata, aes(factor(genderH), (LIMIT_BAL/1000), fill=educationH)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  xlab("Gender") + 
  ylab("BLimit(x1000 NT$)") + 
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Accent")

# Balance limits by education and gender
d2 <- ggplot(ccdata, aes(factor(educationH), (LIMIT_BAL/1000), fill=genderH)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  xlab("Education") + 
  ylab("BLimit(x1000 NT$)") + 
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Paired")

# Balance limits by workstate and education
d3 <-ggplot(ccdata, aes(factor(educationH), (LIMIT_BAL/1000), fill=workstate)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  xlab("Education") + 
  ylab("BLimit(x1000 NT$)") 

I want to use shiny to show, then I want to replace the ''genderH'' and ''educationH'' etc as highlight. I hope I can input those names by selecting in the dashboard. please help, thanks.
I try this one, but it doesn't work:


 tabItem(tabName = "basic",
              h1("Basic Statistics"),
              fluidRow(
                selectInput("select1", label = h3("Select Factor"),
                            choices = list("Workstate" = "workstate", "Gender" = "genderH", "Education" = "educationH","Marital" = "maritalH"),
                            selected = 1)
              selectInput("select2", label = h3("Select Factor"),
                            choices = list("Workstate" = "workstate", "Gender" = "genderH", "Education" = "educationH","Marital" = "maritalH"),
                            selected = 1)
 verticalLayout(plotOutput("plot1", height = 250)),


 service: 
  plot1<-reactive({
    
    d1 <- ggplot(ccdata, aes(factor(select1$input), (LIMIT_BAL/1000), fill=select2$input)) + 
      geom_boxplot() +
      xlab("Gender") + 
      ylab("BLimit(x1000 NT$)") + 
      scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Accent")
    d1
    
    
  })

messages.subject: Re: How to input the "column" name in ggplot? thanks
parts: Let's say you have a column "speed", you'd do aes(speed). But if you have a variable named x that might contain the strings "speed" or "dist", and you want the value to be used as the column, you can't do aes(x) (because that would just look for a column named "x"); instead you'd do aes_string(x), which would look at the value of x to find the column. The same works with any other values you can evaluate, so aes_string(factor(input$select1)) ought to work. (You put input on the right-hand side of the $ multiple times, that's also wrong)
